hints: What ordering do node values have during an in-order traversal of a BST?
Once the values are sorted, do you need to compare every pair?
Keep the previous visited value and update the minimum adjacent difference.
title: Smallest Distance Between BST Nodes

notes: For a BST, an in-order traversal visits node values in strictly increasing order.
Therefore, the smallest difference between any two node values occurs between two consecutive values in the in-order traversal.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 100].
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The in-order traversal is [1,2,3,4,6], so the smallest adjacent difference is 1.
The in-order traversal is [0,1,12,48,49], so the smallest adjacent difference is 1.

content.problemStatement:
With the `root` of a Binary Search Tree (BST), output *the smallest difference between the values of any two different nodes in the tree*.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/02/05/bst1.jpg)

```
Input: root = [4,2,6,1,3]
Output: 1
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/02/05/bst2.jpg)

```
Input: root = [1,0,48,null,null,12,49]
Output: 1
```

**Constraints:**

* The number of nodes in the tree is in the range `[2, 100]`.
* `0 <= Node.val <= 10^5`

**Note:** This question is the same as 530: <https://leetcode.com/problems/smallest-absolute-difference-in-bst/>

notes: Input uses level-order BST serialization with null markers for missing children. Output is one integer.
The recursion-stack equivalent uses O(h) auxiliary space; the supplied boilerplates use an explicit stack, which is also O(h).
solution.approach: Use in-order traversal of the BST. Since the traversal produces node values in increasing order, compare each value only with the previously visited value and keep the smallest difference.

better.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
better.description: Visit all nodes, store their values, sort them, then compare adjacent sorted values.

optimal.complexity: O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: Traverse the BST in-order so the values arrive already sorted. Compare each value with the previous value only; the minimum of these adjacent gaps is the answer.

bruteForce.description: Visit all nodes, store their values, compare every pair, and keep the minimum absolute difference.

followUps: Can you solve it iteratively with an explicit stack?
How would the auxiliary space change for a balanced versus skewed BST?
What changes if duplicate node values are allowed?
